summary: All 20 adversarial tests are valid, technically correct, and target real defect classes in _try_pickup and _on_drop_key. Each test encodes WHY the behavior matters with a docstring explaining what bug it would catch. Tests avoid duplicating existing test_items.py coverage (which focuses on pixel rendering). Adversarial quality is high: boundary conditions, carry-one invariant, mutation bugs, co-located items, rapid cycles, and no-op safety are all covered. All tests pass against the current implementation, confirming the feature is working correctly.

test_assessments.reason: Valid carry-one invariant test. Correctly simulates carrying chalice while overlapping key.
Exhaustive carry-one check for all 6 item-kind pairs. High adversarial value.
Verifies chalice is independently pickupable and removed from floor.
Verifies key is independently pickupable.
Verifies sword is independently pickupable.
Critical: ensures carried slot becomes None after drop.
Ensures dropped item reappears on floor.
Adversarial: catches bug where drop uses original spawn position instead of player position.
Catches dict copy corruption bugs.
Edge case: drop when nothing carried should not modify floor.
High-value adversarial test: catches in-place mutation of carried dict (missing dict() copy).
Integration test: dropped item must be re-pickupable at drop position.
AABB off-by-one: px+ps==item.x should NOT trigger pickup (strict > operator required).
AABB boundary: px+ps==item.x+1 (one pixel overlap) SHOULD trigger pickup.
10-cycle stress test checking carried/floor state consistency throughout.
Catches item duplication or loss bugs across one pickup+drop cycle.
Robustness: empty floor must not crash or corrupt state.
Checks no false-positive pickups from center spawn position.
Data integrity: all 3 item kinds must be present and distinct.
Adversarial: AABB loop should stop after first match — only one item picked up per call.
